subject: general
question: What is the value of an angle subtended by a chord at the centre of the circle, if the angle subtended by this chord at the circumference is 66° ?
solution:
**Given:**

The angle subtended by a chord at the circumference of a circle is 66° .

**Concept used:**

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

**Calculation:**

Let O, R, and PQ be the centre, a point on the circumference, and the chord respectively.

Hence, ∠PRQ = 66°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fec4c898d304005d121bba44ef7fec66d097402b3b1780d018eac22e79814033.png] 

Here, ∠POQ is the angle subtended by the same chord, PQ on the centre of the circle.

According to the concept,

∠POQ = 2 × ∠PRQ

⇒ ∠POQ = 2 × 66°

⇒ ∠POQ = 132°

∴ The angle subtended by the same chord on the centre of the circle is 132°.

**∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.**
